outcome: The question of whether OCA (in the sense most sources mean by the bare name — Todorčević's OCA, OCA_T) is consistent with 2^ℵ₀ > ℵ₂ remains open as of September 2026; no result in the window settles it either way for OCA_T. A distinct but easily confused variant, OCA_ARS (Abraham-Rubin-Shelah), was already shown consistent with 2^ℵ₀=ℵ₃ by Gilton and Neeman, but that paper (arXiv:1904.10516) was first posted in April 2019 and last revised May 2022, entirely before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision, so it is not a change in this window even though it answers a closely related question. A January 2026 preprint by Lorenzo Notaro (arXiv:2601.01166) constructs a model of MA_ℵ1+OCA_T in which Baumgartner's Axiom and OCA_ARS both fail, answering a question of Farah — but this is about Baumgartner's Axiom, not about the size of the continuum, so it does not bear on this bullet.
summary: Wikipedia's bare 'OCA' most commonly refers to Todorčević's Open Coloring Axiom (OCA_T), and the specific open problem — first posed by Todorčević after he showed OCA_T implies b=ℵ2 — is whether OCA_T alone is consistent with 2^ℵ₀ > ℵ₂. This is exactly the question addressed in a 2019 Fields Institute talk by Justin Moore ('Does OCA imply the continuum is ℵ2?'), which states that Moore showed in 2001 that OCA_T + OCA_ARS together force c=ℵ2, but whether OCA_T alone does so (or is consistent with a larger continuum) was open then and — per the 2021 survey 'Ken's colorful questions' (arXiv:2111.00632) and multiple recent secondary sources — remains open through the window. A separate, closely related axiom, OCA_ARS (Abraham-Rubin-Shelah), was shown by Gilton and Neeman to be consistent with 2^ℵ₀=ℵ₃, but that paper (arXiv:1904.10516) was submitted 23 April 2019 and its final revision (v5) posted 17 May 2022 — well before the 26 January 2024 snapshot — so even under a reading where OCA_ARS counts as 'a case of' the bullet's 'OCA', the result predates the window and would be open_stale, not a change in this window. I did not classify it as open_stale for the primary status because the bullet's 'OCA' is more naturally read as OCA_T given the article and survey usage, and the Gilton-Neeman work does not touch OCA_T at all (confirmed by direct fetch of the paper, which never mentions OCA_T). The one item that is new since the frozen date, Lorenzo Notaro's January 2026 arXiv:2601.01166 ('Open Colorings and Baumgartner's Axiom'), works with MA_ℵ1+OCA_T as a hypothesis but proves a result about Baumgartner's Axiom and OCA_ARS failing under that hypothesis — a different question (per §3.1, a related problem, not a restriction of this one) — and does not touch or move the continuum-size question. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this search: all sources are standard human-authored set-theory papers and surveys, with no AI system named, credited, or referenced in any capacity.
competing_reading: If 'OCA' in the Wikipedia bullet is read broadly enough to include OCA_ARS as a legitimate case falling under the same name (the article's own prose does say 'OCA' can refer to either the Todorčević or the Abraham-Rubin-Shelah axiom, and states 'Gilton and Neeman have announced that OCA[ARS] does not imply c=ℵ2'), then the Gilton-Neeman result is a settled case of the bullet — but even under that reading it is dated to 2019 (first posted) / 2022 (final version), both before 26 January 2024, so the correct status would be open_stale rather than any code reflecting a change in this window. Under neither reading does anything in the window (2024-01-26 to 2026-09-22) move this problem.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement that specifically constructs a model of full OCA_T together with 2^ℵ₀ > ℵ₂ (or proves OCA_T implies c=ℵ2), postdating 26 January 2024, would resolve the open problem as stated. Short of that, any explicit new partial result narrowing exactly the OCA_T case (as opposed to OCA_ARS or combinations with Baumgartner's Axiom) would count as partial progress.
